body.statement:
Suppose \(0<\lambda\le1\), so \(\kappa=\lambda\), \(B^4\ge(Sd)^2\), and let \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\).  The total interval \(C_\alpha\) in \texttt{def:honest-interval} satisfies, along every growth array with \(N\wedge T\wedge\min_s n_s\to\infty\),
\[
 \liminf\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 \Pr_P\{\tau(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid z_0\}\ge1-\alpha,
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 \mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid z_0]
 \le C R_\star^{1/2}.
\]
These conclusions use no lower local-modulus condition, count the full-range interval on every declared bad-sample branch, and never divide by an estimated variance.  If \(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(B^4>(Sd)^2\), every random interval \(I_\alpha\) with the same uniform conditional coverage obeys
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 \mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)\mid z_0]
 \ge c R_\star^{1/2}
\]
for all sufficiently large indices.  On the independent-calendar subclass, both upper and lower spacing terms are \(T^{-\lambda/d}\).  The theorem makes no higher-order claim for \(\lambda>1\).
body.justification: The interval concentrates whole bounded unit histories after conditioning on design and donors, then adds Holder and full-covariance donor radii.  Armstrong--Kolesar ordered-modulus and bias-aware intervals concern ordinary regression, while Cattaneo--Feng--Titiunik study dependent synthetic-control prediction; neither supplies this generated-query causal expected-length frontier.
body.gap: The donor expected-length converse requires strict interior and moment slack, and the interval does not attain exact phase-intersection constants.
body.consumer: The procedure is conditionally honest without calendar-score decoupling and remains covering on every declared fallback.
body.proof_tex:
Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification} gives the observed-law functional, and bounded wealth gives \(\tau(z_0)\in[-2B,2B]\).  We first prove coverage on the regular branch.  Since \(0<\lambda\le1\), one has \(r=0\).  Conditional on the exact design and the donor sample, all selected weights are response-independent, nonnegative, and satisfy \(\sum_t w_{st}=1\).  For each unit history define
\[
 \xi_{si}=\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\left[
 B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0)
 -\sum_{t=1}^{T}w_{st}\{Q_{sti}-m_s(X_{st})\}\right].
\tag{1}
\]
By \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation}, the donor sample is conditionally independent of the complete joint panel given \(z_0\).  Therefore conditioning further on the donor sample does not change the conditional law of the unit histories given \((z_0,X)\).  The two equalities in \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} center (1), and \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence} makes the \(\xi_{si}\)'s independent across \((s,i)\).  Their range lengths are at most
\[
 d_{si}=\frac{2B\pi_s}{n_s}\left(1+\sum_{t=1}^{T}|w_{st}|\right).
\tag{2}
\]
For a variable \(V\in[a,b]\), convexity of the exponential gives \(\mathbb E\exp\{u(V-\mathbb EV)\}\le\exp\{u^2(b-a)^2/8\}\).  Exponential Markov optimization, independence, and (2) therefore imply
\[
 \Pr\left\{\left|\sum_{s,i}\xi_{si}\right|>r_{\mathrm{unit}}
       \mathrel{\Big|}z_0,X,(Z_j)_j\right\}
 \le2\exp\{-4\log(8/\alpha_{\mathrm{st}})\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}.
\tag{3}
\]
The positive linear term in \(r_{\mathrm{unit}}\) only enlarges the radius.  Notice that (3) treats the complete vector \((Q_{sti})_{t=1}^{T}\) and the event outcome as one bounded unit-history variable; it neither conditions on response blocks nor asserts calendar-score independence.

For the donor event, spectral clipping gives \(\widehat\Sigma\succeq(c_\Sigma/2)I_q\), where \(q=Sd\).  Every fold has size at least \(N/3\), so donor unbiasedness and the upper covariance bound imply
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[N\|\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}
   (\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2^2\mid z_0\right]
 \le\frac{6qC_\Sigma}{c_\Sigma}.
\tag{4}
\]
This uses only the deterministic eigenvalue bound on the clipped matrix and does not require independence between the sample mean and covariance estimate.  Markov's inequality, a union bound over at most two folds, and the definition of \(q_{\mathrm{don}}\) give
\[
 \Pr\left\{\max_\ell\|\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}
  (\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2>q_{\mathrm{don}}N^{-1/2}\mid z_0\right\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{5}
\]
On the complement, the upper clipping bound and nonexpansiveness of cube projection imply \(\max_\ell\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2\le CN^{-1/2}\).  At any selected local-constant fit, nonnegative unit-mass weights and kernel support give
\[
 \left|\sum_t w_{st}^{(\ell)}m_s(X_{st})-m_s(\widetilde z_{\ell s})\right|
 \le C\{\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
           +\widehat h_{s\ell}^\lambda\}.
\tag{6}
\]
Holder continuity between \(\widetilde z_{\ell s}\) and \(z_{0s}\), (5), and the defining domination property of \(C_H\) show that the total deterministic error is at most \(r_{\mathrm{bias}}+r_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Combining (3), (5), and \(\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}=\alpha\) proves coverage on the regular branch.  On every declared bad branch \(C_\alpha=[-2B,2B]\), which contains the target.  Intersecting a covering interval with this known target range preserves coverage.  Thus the displayed asymptotic uniform coverage follows; no calendar-score radius is used.

We next bound expected length.  On the regular branch, \(\sum_t|w_{st}|=1\), whence
\[
 r_{\mathrm{samp}}=r_{\mathrm{unit}}\le C(\alpha,B)A^{1/2},
 \qquad A=\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}.
\tag{7}
\]
Indeed, the square-root term is immediate and \(\max_s\pi_s/n_s\le A^{1/2}\).  Whenever the reference anchor is available, selected-certificate optimality gives
\[
 r_{\mathrm{bias}}
 \le C\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\left\{(h_s^\star)^\lambda
 +K_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^\lambda\right\}.
\tag{8}
\]
Donor unbiasedness, ellipticity, projection nonexpansiveness, and Jensen's inequality yield
\[
 \mathbb E(\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^\lambda\mid z_0)
 \le CN^{-\lambda/2}.
\tag{9}
\]
Taking expectations in (8) and applying the query-conditional moment bound \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} gives
\[
\begin{split}
 \sup_P\mathbb E_P(r_{\mathrm{bias}}+r_{\mathrm{don}}\mid z_0)
 \le C\bigg[&\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
 +\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{\lambda/d}
 +N^{-\lambda/2}\bigg].
\end{split}
\tag{10}
\]
Along the stated growth arrays the deterministic small-sample branches disappear.  The fixed-scale part of the anchor lemma bounds the remaining unavailable-reference event by \(CT^{-2}\); interval length is always at most \(4B\).  Equations (7)--(10) and the smoothing domination in \texttt{thm:marginal-phase-diagram} imply
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 \mathbb E_P\{\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid z_0\}
 \le CR_\star^{1/2}.
\tag{11}
\]
On \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{iid}}_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), the independent part of the anchor lemma replaces the logarithmic term by \(T^{-\lambda/d}\).

For the converse, suppose two laws with targets \(\theta_0,\theta_1\) possess a common subprobability measure \(\nu\) of mass \(\eta>2\alpha\).  Uniform conditional coverage \(1-\alpha-o(1)\) under both laws gives
\[
 \nu\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I_\alpha\}\ge\eta-2\alpha-o(1).
\]
Every interval on this event has length at least \(|\theta_1-\theta_0|\), and therefore
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)
 \ge|\theta_1-\theta_0|\{\eta-2\alpha-o(1)\}.
\tag{12}
\]
Embed the treated pair (9)--(10) of \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier} in the causal class using query-conditionally independent uniform designs, constant untreated surfaces, an admissible common donor law independent of the complete panel, and positive translated event outcomes, exactly as in the treated-channel construction of \texttt{thm:marginal-phase-diagram}.  This verifies the replacement design assumptions, consistency, event-date transport, and the buy-and-hold representation.  Choose \(\gamma\) small enough that the pair's common mass exceeds \(2\alpha\); (12) then gives \(cA^{1/2}\).

For the donor channel, apply \texttt{lem:full-covariance-location-pair} with \(\eta\in(2\alpha,1)\), and embed its pair in the causal class as follows.  Draw the exact designs conditionally independently and uniformly, independently of the fixed realized path and the donors.  Use in the displaced cohort a positive bounded regression \(m(x)=b_0+a_0|x_k-z_{0k}|^\lambda\), use constants in the other cohorts, set \(Q_{sti}=m_s(X_{st})\), take a common positive constant treated wealth, and set untreated event wealth equal to \(m_s(z_s)\).  Choosing \(a_0,b_0\) small puts all wealth and regressions in the prescribed bounds and Holder ball.  With \(W_{si,-1}=1\), horizon-zero return equal to potential wealth minus one, and later returns zero, the buy-and-hold identity, consistency, and event-date transport hold.  The design is query-conditionally uniform and independent, unit histories are independent, and donors factor from the complete panel.  Thus both laws belong to the repaired base class, their observed panel coordinates coincide, their donor laws have common mass at least \(\eta\), and their targets differ by \(cN^{-\lambda/2}\).  Equation (12) gives the donor lower bound \(cN^{-\lambda/2}\).

Finally, \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} supplies, for the stated \(\alpha\), common mass above \(2\alpha\) and target separation \(c\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{\lambda/d}\) under the repaired conditional design assumptions.  Equation (12), followed by smoothing domination, yields \(cR_\star^{1/2}\).  On the conditionally independent-calendar subclass, the no-hit construction (6) in \texttt{thm:marginal-phase-diagram}, with its cube chosen small enough that its common mass exceeds \(2\alpha\), gives the corresponding \(T^{-\lambda/d}\) lower bound.  This completes the coverage, expected-length, and converse claims.
